\paragraph{Provenance and limits} The English questions and gold aliases were written against the source text. The Sinhala, Tamil, and code-switched questions were first drafted by machine translation and then reviewed by a native speaker of Sinhala and Tamil (the author), who rated all 146 non-English queries as faithful, reworded, or rewritten against the English source and checked that the gold aliases cover the natural answer in that language (Sinhala: all 62 accepted unchanged; Tamil: all 62 accepted unchanged; code-switched: all 22 accepted unchanged). No query or alias list was changed; the review sheet is released with the benchmark. The review was done by a single reviewer who is also the author, so it rules out mistranslation but is not an independent inter-annotator study. The Sinhala and Tamil summaries inside the corpus documents, which carry the numbers the non-English queries are answered from, have not been reviewed by a native speaker (a review sheet is provided). The corpus is small by design, so that every fact is traceable to a government URL; it does not measure retrieval at scale.
